newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ANZ's Mercer says Costello criticism crazy.
newsitem.headline: ANZ's Mercer says Costello criticism crazy.

text.p: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd (ANZ) chief executive officer Don Mercer on Sunday accused Treasurer Peter Costello of "crazy talk" in criticising the banks' handling of recent interest rate cuts.
Mercer had been asked in a television interview about Costello's suggestion that more competition would force the banks to give a better deal to customers.
"I think that's crazy talk. I just don't understand that statement," Mercer said.

"You couldn't introduce more competition and the idea of it being a punishment, I mean, it's really quite offensive," he said. "The market, believe me, is pretty competitive already and more competition is just more of the same," he said.

Australia's major banks have come under fire for passing on just 0.35 of a percentage point of the Reserve Bank's 0.50 point cut in official cash rates to 5.5 percent on May 23. The ANZ later cut its rate by another 20 points.
The uniform cut in rates by the banks after the official cut also aroused the suspicions of the Australian Consumer and Competition Commission, the country's anti-monopolies regulator.
The banks have denied any collusion on rates.

"If you look at the facts of what's happened this last time it's interesting that in February the Commonwealth Bank moved 70 points down, there was no movement in official rates at all, but the Commonwealth for competitive reasons moved 70 points," Mercer said.
"We matched it for competitive reasons and everybody said 'whoopee, the market's working, isn't this good'.

"This time, when rates moved 50 points and we matched the market, the first mover was the Commonwealth again at 7.20 (per cent) everybody said 'collusion, this is sinful, you haven't moved', Mercer said in the interview on the Nine Network.
"As I see the evidence, the banks have moved 105 points since Christmas, the cash rate's gone 50," he said.
The Reserve Bank of Australia has cut interest rates by a total of two percentage points since July 1996.

The ANZ announced last week that its net profit rose to A$615 million in the six months to March 31, up 18 percent from A$520 million a year earlier. The bank also announced that Mercer would retire at year-end.
